newsitem.title: PERU: POLL - Lima mayor dwarfs Fujimori in popularity.
newsitem.headline: POLL - Lima mayor dwarfs Fujimori in popularity.

text.p: Lima Mayor Alberto Andrade is more than twice as popular as Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori and would beat him if a general election were held now, according to an opinion poll published Monday.
The University of Lima survey gave a 70.3 percent approval rating to Andrade compared with 33.9 percent for Fujimori.
The poll of 400 people in Lima also showed that if an election were held tomorrow, 29.4 percent would vote for Andrade whereas only 20.2 percent would vote for Fujimori.

The figures were in line with other recent polls showing Fujimori's tumble in popularity since his 67 percent approval rating after the April 22 siege that ended the Lima hostage crisis, in which 72 hostages were held by leftist Tupac Amaru rebels in the Japanese ambassador's residence.

Andrade, who has served as mayor of Peru's capital city since 1995, returned to a hero's welcome Sunday after a tour of Europe and Russia. A large crowd of supporters from his newly formed political party, Somos Peru (We are Peru), cheered him as he left the Lima airport.
Andrade confirmed he would run for re-election in 1998, but he would not comment on whether he would seek the presidency in the year 2000.
Fujimori's popularity has held in the low 30s in recent weeks amid strong criticism of his government's perceived authoritarianism.

That perception caused 56.6 percent of those surveyed to say Peruvians lived under a dictatorship, 81.5 percent to say that Congress did not respect the constitution and 68.3 percent to disapprove of the performance of Congress.
Congress has been criticized for its dismissal last month of three constitutional judges who were blocking a possible re-election bid by Fujimori in 2000.
No margin of error was given for the poll, which was taken on June 25.
